body:
Frozen means "has voted to close, or is no longer a member" (wire contract, The freeze). Both clients label every frozen participant's row with expense.frozen / expense_frozen: "agreed to close — amounts fixed", which is false for someone who simply left. The web's save-time message expense.error.frozen ("{who} has agreed to close the list, so their amounts cannot change") has the same problem. expense.deleteBlocked already gets it right ("involves someone whose amounts are fixed").

Fix: neutral wording, or two strings chosen by why the person is frozen, on both clients and in all nine locales.

Also: expense.error.frozen exists on the web only and crossClient.test.ts still passes, so a web-only string is not caught by the parity check. Either add the Android counterpart (see the Android refusal-surfacing ticket) or make the test fail on one-sided strings.
title: 'agreed to close — amounts fixed' is shown for former members who never voted; web-only string escaped the parity test
